events.title: .NET 6 LTS released
events.summary: Microsoft shipped .NET 6 on November 8, 2021 — a long-term support release unifying mobile, cloud, and desktop with minimal APIs and hot reload.
events.about: .NET 6 succeeded .NET 5 as the modern default: MAUI for mobile/desktop, Blazor for web, and performance gains across the stack. LTS status through 2024 made it the enterprise migration target after .NET Framework's sunset.

narrative.whyChosen: .NET 6 was the first LTS after the unified .NET branding settled.
narrative.whyImportant: One SDK for cloud, mobile, and desktop reduced platform fragmentation.
narrative.problemSolved: Teams hesitated on .NET 5 without LTS guarantees for production workloads.

events.title: C# 10 released with .NET 6
events.summary: C# 10 shipped with .NET 6 on November 8, 2021 — adding file-scoped namespaces, record structs, global usings, and `InterpolatedStringHandler`.
events.about: C# 10 reduced boilerplate: `namespace X;` replaced brace blocks; `global using` cleaned up imports; record structs brought value semantics to small types. Interpolated string handlers enabled zero-allocation formatting in hot paths.

narrative.whyChosen: C# 10's file-scoped namespaces and global usings cleaned up everyday .NET code.
narrative.whyImportant: Less ceremony accelerated adoption of minimal hosting and top-level programs.
narrative.problemSolved: Namespace braces and repetitive using statements cluttered modern C# files.

events.title: GHC 9.2 released
events.summary: The Glasgow Haskell Compiler 9.2.1 shipped on November 6, 2021 with improved compile times, unboxed sums, and better Windows support.
events.about: GHC 9.2 refined the post-9.0 compiler with faster builds for large Haskell codebases and language extensions used in production (Cardano, Jane Street tooling). It bridged teams on GHC 8.10 toward the 9.x line.

narrative.whyChosen: GHC 9.2 was the stability release that encouraged production upgrades from GHC 8.
narrative.whyImportant: Compile-time improvements kept Haskell viable for large industrial codebases.
narrative.problemSolved: Teams hesitated to move off GHC 8.x due to build-time regressions in early 9.0.
